content.user_title: Build Real-Time Voice Apps with Azure .NET
content.value_statement: Real-time voice applications require coordinated authentication, audio streaming, event handling, and session configuration. This skill provides practical .NET guidance for Azure AI Voice Live workflows.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the Azure AI Voice Live, Azure Identity, and NAudio packages needed for a .NET project.
Explains Microsoft Entra ID and API key authentication for Azure Voice Live clients.
Configures models, voices, modalities, PCM audio formats, and semantic voice activity detection.
Processes streamed audio, text, function-call, completion, and error events from a Voice Live session.
Sends user messages and starts responses through the Voice Live session API.
Defines function tools and returns function results to an active voice conversation.
limitations: The skill provides reference guidance, not a complete runnable application or deployment template.
An Azure resource, valid credentials, assigned roles, and network access are required.
Preview model names and SDK versions can change, so current Azure documentation must be checked.
Audio device capture, playback, and external function services require additional implementation.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Voice Assistant
use_cases.description: Create a basic .NET session that receives text and audio responses from Azure AI Voice Live.
use_cases.target_user: C# developers evaluating real-time voice AI

use_cases.title: Add Voice to Support Software
use_cases.description: Plan event handling, voice activity detection, and response streaming for an interactive support application.
use_cases.target_user: Application teams building customer support tools

use_cases.title: Integrate Voice Functions
use_cases.description: Connect a Voice Live conversation to approved business functions and return results during the session.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up a Basic Project
prompt_templates.prompt: List the packages, Azure prerequisites, environment variables, and authentication steps for a new .NET Azure AI Voice Live project.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when starting a Voice Live project.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a Voice Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Voice Live session using [model], [voice], PCM16 audio, text and audio modalities, and semantic voice activity detection.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when selecting session settings.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Streaming Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a C# event-processing approach for audio deltas, text deltas, function calls, completion events, errors, cancellation, and session disposal.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when implementing the response loop.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Function-Enabled Assistant
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a production Voice Live assistant that calls [business function]. Include argument validation, authorization, error handling, observability, and safe response delivery.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for an advanced tool-enabled voice workflow.

output_examples.input: Explain the minimum setup for a new Voice Live application.
output: Add the Voice Live and Azure Identity packages.
Create an Azure AI resource and assign the Cognitive Services User role.
Store the endpoint in configuration and authenticate with DefaultAzureCredential.
Start a session, then configure text, audio, voice, and turn detection.

output_examples.input: What events should my response loop process?
output_examples.output: Process audio and text deltas, function-call requests, completion notifications, and errors. Dispose the session when the conversation ends.

output_examples.input: How should I configure voice activity detection?
output_examples.output: Use semantic voice activity detection and tune threshold, prefix padding, and silence duration with representative audio from the target environment.

best_practices: Prefer DefaultAzureCredential and assign only the required Cognitive Services role.
Handle every expected session event and dispose the session after use.
Test voice activity detection and audio settings with representative devices and background noise.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode API keys in source code, prompts, logs, or configuration committed to version control.
Do not execute function calls without validating arguments and authorizing the requested action.
Do not assume preview model names, voice availability, or SDK behavior remain unchanged.

faq.question: Which .NET packages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure.AI.VoiceLive and Azure.Identity, with NAudio suggested for audio capture and playback.

faq.question: Which authentication method is recommended?
faq.answer: Microsoft Entra ID with DefaultAzureCredential is recommended. The Azure resource also needs the Cognitive Services User role.

faq.question: Does the skill provide a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides focused examples for setup, sessions, events, messages, functions, errors, and audio configuration.

faq.question: Which audio format does the guidance use?
faq.answer: The examples use 16-bit PCM input and output, a 24 kHz sample rate, and mono audio.

faq.question: Can the assistant call external functions?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill shows how to define a function, receive arguments, and return a function result to the session.

faq.question: What must be verified before production use?
faq.answer: Verify current SDK versions, model availability, voice support, credentials, authorization, error behavior, latency, and audio quality.
